 TV Shows Published November 11, 2026 Meet the Maximoffs: Joe Locke Interviews His ‘VisionQuest’ Brother Ruaridh Mollica 
 The ‘VisionQuest’ actors behind Billy Kaplan and Tommy Shepherd talk about their on-screen familial bond, online fan theories, and keeping Marvel secrets. 
 BY Devan Coggan 
 Warning: This article contains spoilers for the  VisionQuest finale. 
 The Maximoff boys are back together again. 
 The final episode of Marvel Television’s VisionQuest  reunites brothers Thomas Shepherd ( Ruaridh Mollica ) and Billy Kaplan ( Joe Locke ), the twin sons of Wanda Maximoff ( Elizabeth Olsen ) and Vision ( Paul Bettany ). Born in the magical chaos of WandaVision , both boys were separated after the Westview hex dispersed, until Billy’s spirit was transferred into the body of American teenager William Kaplan. In Agatha All Along , Billy used his witch powers to move his brother Tommy's consciousness into dying Scottish teen Thomas Shepherd, and the pair have been trying to get back to each other ever since.
 The VisionQuest  finale finds the two boys reconnecting at last. Together, they use their respective powers — reality-bending magic for Billy and super speed for Tommy — to help save their dad Vision from Ultron ( James Spader ) and his world-ending scheme. It’s a long-awaited homecoming for both the characters and the actors who play them: Off screen, Mollica and Locke have become close friends, starring together in last year’s West End production of the play Clarkston.   
 To celebrate Billy and Tommy’s reunion, Locke and Mollica sat down for a delightful Maximoff family conversation, where they opened up about joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe and their real-life brotherly bond.
 Billy (Joe Locke) and Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica) in 'VisionQuest' JOE LOCKE: Hi, Ruaridh.
 RUARIDH MOLLICA: Hi, Joe Locke.
 JOE LOCKE: As you know, you’re joining the MCU for the first time. I thought it’d be really good just to interview you and check that you’re right for the role. I know you’ve already got the role, but to join the Maximoff family, I feel like you need to pass some tests. So, a lot of people don’t know that we did a play together last year, but we actually met before that. Did you tell anyone?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Yeah, we met on set for VisionQuest . Well, we did go for like a boozy brunch the week before, and then we met on set for VisionQuest . Instead of running our lines for our [ VisionQuest ] scene, we ran the lines for the auditions for the play that was the next day, where we played lovers.
 JOE LOCKE:  Brothers to lovers.
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Brothers to lovers, and then back to brothers. It sounds like an Adele song or something.
 JOE LOCKE:  How did you react when you first found out you got the role?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  I cried. I just couldn’t believe it, do you know what I mean? You can’t believe it, and then your mind starts racing. Then, when you get over that sheer, adrenaline-fueled excitement, then you have to be like, “Oh my God, now I actually have to do the job.” And that’s where the challenge comes in.
 JOE LOCKE:  I actually knew they were looking at casting you before you got the role.
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Really? 
 JOE LOCKE:  [Producer] Mary Livanos texted me and said, “What do you think about this guy?”
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  No way! What did you say?
 JOE LOCKE:  I said, “He’s… awful.”
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Oh, I knew it.
 JOE LOCKE:  I said, “He’s just… smelly. I can smell him from here.” [ Laughs ]
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  I am  really sweaty. 
 JOE LOCKE:  No, not that I had any power over whether they cast you. But I’m reading here that it was Paul who encouraged you to use your native Scottish accent, is that right? I’m really jealous that I didn’t get to use mine. 
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  I know. Imagine you got to do your Manx accent. That would’ve been so cool. But it feels really nice to do my own voice. It feels closer to me. I still don’t know whether Paul said that because my English accent was so bad. [ Laughs ]
 JOE LOCKE:  I’ve actually never heard your English accent.
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  And you never will! [ Laughs ]
 Ruaridh Mollica, Paul Bettany, and Joe Locke in 'VisionQuest' JOE LOCKE:  How does it feel having the worst superpower in the Maximoff family?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Well, I don’t know, I guess I’d have to ask you that question, Joe.
 JOE LOCKE:  That’s interesting because I actually think that I have a much better superpower than you. Can you fly?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  You know, I think if I ran fast enough…
 JOE LOCKE:  But can you fly ? Can you create whole altered universes of realities with your brain? 
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Well, at least my  character’s not a narcissist. [ Laughs ]
 JOE LOCKE:  Fine, back to some normal questions. [ Laughs ] What was your most memorable day on set?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Our days [together] got to be memorable because we practiced for the play, and then we got to do our scenes of those worlds colliding between your show and my show. Plus, the secret of you coming back.
 JOE LOCKE:  Was there anything that surprised you about joining the Marvel universe?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Probably how much care and passion is behind it all. It was a deeply human and emotionally dramatic story, which isn’t what I imagined going into it. It ended up  being some of the hardest scenes emotionally I’ve ever had to act. 
 JOE LOCKE:  I think when you join something as huge as this on this scale, you just assume it’s some machine. But getting to see it made, I had the same experience of [discovering] that it’s actually the most creative process. And what was it like getting to work with Paul Bettany? What an icon. 
 RUARIDH MOLLICA: I know I mean, I instantly bonded with him in that father and son relationship, which was lovely. I literally arrived at the screen test and was like, “I love you.” [ Laughs ] We just got closer and closer over the shoot, which was so lovely. And if I had any questions about the MCU, I mean…
 JOE LOCKE:  What better person to ask?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  It was so lovely. 
 Joe Locke, Paul Bettany, and Ruaridh Mollica attend a special screening of 'VisionQuest' JOE LOCKE:  What’s your favorite thing about being in the MCU?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Normally, you make something and you let the fans into it as a new world. But this is the first time where you’re making something that already exists, and it’s like you’re giving it to the fans as a gift. You hope that they like it, and they enjoy it, and that you’ve done an accurate representation of what they’ve grown up with or seen or read in comics. That’s been a really novel experience for me.
 JOE LOCKE:  It’s quite daunting. It’s that thing of wanting to live up to their expectations but also wanting it to be your own as well. 
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Totally. It’s walking that line of: How do I bring my own spin to this? And I think we both did. 
 JOE LOCKE:  That’s the great bit of it, that the fans on the whole are very supportive of you making it yours. And we definitely have.
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  We had a lot of creative license because we were both put into the bodies of new people, which was good. 
 JOE LOCKE:  What kind of research did you do for this?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  I watched all of WandaVision,  which was great. I imagine you did the same thing, right? That’s all of [Tommy and Billy’s] memories.
 JOE LOCKE:  Hmm, you didn’t watch all of Agatha All Along ?
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Uhhh… [ Laughs ] No, of course I did. I loved that show.
 JOE LOCKE:  What if you were like, “No, I actually avoided that one.”
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  “Yeah, I knew you were in it, so I didn’t watch it.” But obviously, the first thing I did was get all the comics where our characters were on the front. I also read so many fan theories on Reddit, just because I really wanted to see what people wanted.
 JOE LOCKE:  It’s crazy how accurate they can be sometimes.
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  I know! Sometimes people say stuff, and I’m like, “How do you know that?! We’ve not even shot that yet!” 
 JOE LOCKE:  Have you found keeping all the secrets hard? 
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Definitely.
 JOE LOCKE:  Do you remember when we were doing the play, and we had a Q&A after? We had obviously met on set filming our scenes, and we’d maybe let it slip to the director of our play that had happened. We were doing a Q&A, and he was so adamant like, “Well, you guys [already] filmed together…” And we were like, “No! No we didn’t! [ Laughs ]
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  That was scary! [ Laughs ]
 JOE LOCKE:  But look, here we are!
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  Here we are! We didn’t get fired! Well, it’s a bit late now. They already filmed the show.
 JOE LOCKE:  We didn’t get fired! [ Laughs ] But I’m so proud of you, Ruaridh. I think that everyone is going to absolutely love VisionQuest , and I’m just so happy that you’re my brother.
 RUARIDH MOLLICA:  I’m happy that you’re my  brother. I love you.
 Marvel Television’s  VisionQuest   is streaming now, exclusively on Disney+.
